analysis.successDefinition: Three new test files exist under packages/llm-http-proxy/src/ (one per provider, SDK-specific) that (1) follow the verbatim RUN_BENCH-style `if (hasKey) describe(...) else describe.skip(...)` gate from src/benchmark.test.ts:359-366 with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, and GEMINI_API_KEY (GOOGLE_API_KEY fallback) as the gate vars; (2) build an `Interceptor`, call `install()`, run the SDK's standard generation call, await two setImmediate ticks before asserting, and `restore()` in a `finally`-equivalent discipline mirroring src/interceptor.test.ts:75-91; (3) assert on captured LlmLogEntry fields (model, url, token counts) — never on callerTrace — and assert `JSON.stringify(entries[0])` excludes the literal apiKey value; (4) install `ai` + `@ai-sdk/anthropic` + `@ai-sdk/openai` + `@ai-sdk/google` as devDependencies only (no `dependencies` or `peerDependencies` entries, no exports from src/index.ts, package-lock.json gitignored per the zero-lockfile convention). Default `npm test` from packages/llm-http-proxy/ must pass with zero network egress and zero credentials; with each key set, the corresponding SDK suite must run and pass against the real provider endpoint; the post-addition baseline test count and wall-clock must stay within the horizon-7-recorded ms-scale skip-overhead budget.
assumptions: The Vercel AI SDK exposes a documented `fetch` option on each provider factory (anthropic, openai, google) that accepts a custom fetch implementation; passing a node:https.request-backed shim as this option makes SDK traffic flow through http.ClientRequest.prototype, which the interceptor already patches.

The horizon-7 raw-HTTPS integration test files (packages/llm-http-proxy/src/{anthropic,openai,gemini}.integration.test.ts) are the authoritative templates — same key-gate shape (no LIVE flag, env-var presence IS the gate), same env-driven baseUrl/model overrides, same two-setImmediate flush, same `JSON.stringify` no-key safety assertion, same `capturePayloads` default-off discipline.

Empty-string env vars (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=` exported by a CI matrix) are treated as unset and resolve to `describe.skip`, matching horizon7's gate convention and the existing local `string | undefined` + `length > 0` check.

Gemini's SDK call uses header auth (`x-goog-api-key`) rather than URL-query `?key=` so the horizon-7 URL-key-safety rubric (`entries[0].url` must not contain the apiKey) holds without an interceptor change.

The package's zero-lockfile convention (per the horizon-6 discovery on peer dep install) is preserved by gitignoring any package-lock.json produced by the new devDependency install — no lockfile is committed.

The post-horizon-8 baseline wall-clock for default `npm test` stays within ms-scale skip-overhead of horizon-7's 127-test / ~1.4s-ish recorded time; describe.skip overhead does not measurably creep across three additional gated files.

discoveryFindings.finding: Node's built-in global fetch (Node 18+) is implemented on top of undici and does NOT flow through http.ClientRequest.prototype. Monkey-patching http.ClientRequest.prototype.write/end intercepts only the node:http and node:https APIs. When Vercel AI SDK calls the global fetch (its default transport), the request is constructed via undici's Dispatcher / Client internals and the current patch surface never sees it. The Vercel AI SDK does expose a `fetch` option on each provider factory that lets a caller substitute a custom fetch implementation, so a wrapper that calls node:https.request under the hood WOULD be captured.
discoveryFindings.implication: The horizon must wrap the SDK's `fetch` option with a node:https.request shim (option B from the discovery) — turning each SDK test into a self-validating capture harness. Option (a) is empirically broken; option (c) undici Dispatcher patching is out of scope.

discoveryFindings.finding: The horizon-7 discoveries file claims 'engines.node >=18; global fetch routes through http.ClientRequest.prototype under Node 18+'. That claim is empirically wrong for Node 18+ — fetch is undici-backed. The horizon-7 fetch-baseline test was contractually rewritten to use `https.request` from node:https instead of global fetch.
discoveryFindings.implication: A future horizon revisiting fetch-interception must either use the node:https path (this horizon's approach) or extend the interceptor to patch undici; do not trust the unverified horizon-7 discovery entry.

discoveryFindings.finding: Confirmed at /Users/dimitrykatz/workspace/elenwatch/packages/llm-http-proxy/src/interceptor.ts:225-228 that the patch surface is http.ClientRequest.prototype (write/end/on), install() patches once process-wide. This covers node:http and node:https traffic; it does NOT cover undici's internal Client / Dispatcher that backs Node's global fetch.
discoveryFindings.implication: The shim's transport MUST be node:https.request to land on the patched surface; any other transport would silently bypass capture.

discoveryFindings.finding: All three horizon-7 raw-HTTPS integration tests use the verbatim gate `if (hasKey) describe(...) else describe.skip(...)` pattern with apiKey read as `string | undefined` and empty-string treated as unset (length > 0 check). They each build an Interceptor with `providers: [parsedUrl.hostname]`, call node:https.request directly, await two setImmediate ticks after res.on('end'), assert entries.length === 1 plus model/url/token assertions, and assert JSON.stringify(entries[0]) does not contain the apiKey.
discoveryFindings.implication: The verbatim gate shape is portable; the SDK tests copy the gate verbatim. The two-setImmediate flush, the install/restore try/finally discipline, the providers:[hostname] scoping, the JSON.stringify no-key safety assertion, and the captured-on-fields-only assertion surface are all reusable.

discoveryFindings.finding: The `ai` package is the meta-SDK entry; per-provider companion packages are `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, `@ai-sdk/openai`, `@ai-sdk/google`. Each provider factory exposes a `fetch: (input, init) => Promise<Response>` option that accepts a custom fetch implementation — this is the official interception seam per the AI SDK cookbook. Engines require Node 18+ for v5; main entry is ESM-first.
discoveryFindings.implication: Installable as devDependencies without raising the engines bar. The custom `fetch` option is the documented escape hatch the horizon must use.

discoveryFindings.finding: /Users/dimitrykatz/workspace/elenwatch/packages/llm-http-proxy/tsconfig.json has `types: ['node', 'jest']` and uses `@types/node@22` + `@types/jest@29`. The `ai` and `@ai-sdk/*` packages ship with their own TypeScript types and declare their peer types via package.json, so adding them as devDependencies typechecks under tsc with the existing types:['node','jest'] list — no extra @types/* packages required.
discoveryFindings.implication: No tsconfig changes or extra @types packages are required to make the SDK packages compile.

discoveryFindings.finding: The Vercel AI SDK is NOT installed anywhere in this repo. There is no entry for `ai` or `@ai-sdk/*` in /Users/dimitrykatz/workspace/elenwatch/packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json. The packages/llm-http-proxy/node_modules directory has no `ai` folder and no `@ai-sdk` scope.

discoveryFindings.finding: /Users/dimitrykatz/workspace/elenwatch/packages/llm-http-proxy/.gitignore contains `package_modules/`, `dist/`, `coverage/`, `*.log`, and `package-lock.json`. The repo root .gitignore does NOT list `package-lock.json` but the package-local .gitignore covers it. pnpm-lock.yaml is the committed lockfile for the package (and the repo root), not package-lock.json.

discoveryFindings.finding: The gemini test (src/gemini.integration.test.ts) uses header auth (`x-goog-api-key`) and asserts BOTH `entries[0].url not.toContain(apiKey)` AND `JSON.stringify(entries[0]) not.toContain(apiKey)`. The deriveUrl() implementation in src/interceptor.ts:924-963 passes req.path verbatim and would leak any URL-query auth into entries[0].url.
discoveryFindings.implication: The SDK gemini test must use `@ai-sdk/google`'s default header-based auth; if the SDK defaults change to query-param, the URL-key safety rubric would fail.

discoveryFindings.finding: src/provider-parser.ts:141-152 defaultParser extracts model from `model` then `model_name`, input via ceil(chars/4), output via usage.completion_tokens (OpenAI shape) > usage.output_tokens (Anthropic shape) > chars/4 fallback. The Gemini response shape uses `usageMetadata` (camelCase) with `promptTokenCount` / `candidatesTokenCount` — NOT recognized by the default parser, outputTokens falls back to chars/4.
discoveryFindings.implication: For the SDK gemini test, the existing horizon-7 rubric's `expect(entries[0].outputTokens).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0)` assertion still holds (the chars/4 fallback is non-negative), but the assertion is no longer meaningful — the SDK test should mirror horizon-7's >=0 assertion shape.

phases.name: Install SDK packages as devDependencies
phases.goal: Add the Vercel AI SDK packages to packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json as devDependencies only, with no entries added to dependencies or peerDependencies.
phases.rationale: The Vercel AI SDK's default transport is Node's global fetch (undici-backed in Node 18+), which does NOT flow through the http.ClientRequest prototype that the interceptor patches. Without installing the SDK as a test-only dependency, none of the later per-provider test phases can run. Adding the SDK packages as devDependencies only preserves the zero-hard-deps public surface invariant — the published tarball still ships with `dependencies: {}` so consumers of llm-http-proxy never need the SDK installed.
changes: Add `ai`, `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, `@ai-sdk/openai`, and `@ai-sdk/google` (v5.x stable) to the `devDependencies` block of packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json; do not add to `dependencies` or `peerDependencies`.

Run the install with the package manager whose lockfile is committed at the repo root (per the .gitignore audit in the zero-lockfile discovery) and confirm any generated package-lock.json is gitignored at the package level.
inputs: Stage 1 outOfScope list items `zero-hard-deps public surface` and `zero-lockfile convention`
phases.expectedResult: packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json lists `ai` plus `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, `@ai-sdk/openai`, and `@ai-sdk/google` in devDependencies; `dependencies` and `peerDependencies` remain unchanged from their current empty/OTEL-only state.
phases.compensation: Revert by removing the four entries from package.json devDependencies and uninstalling the npm packages.

rubric.label: SDK packages live in devDependencies only
rubric.ruleStatement: The four Vercel AI SDK packages must appear in the devDependencies block of packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json and must not appear in dependencies or peerDependencies.
passCriteria: Open packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json and confirm the devDependencies block lists all four keys: `ai`, `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, `@ai-sdk/openai`, `@ai-sdk/google` with non-empty version strings.
Confirm the dependencies block contains none of those four keys.
Confirm the peerDependencies block contains none of those four keys.
Each listed version string starts with `5.` (e.g., `^5.x.y` or `5.x.y`).
failureExamples: `ai` appears under `dependencies` instead of `devDependencies`.
Only three of the four SDK packages are listed; `@ai-sdk/google` is missing from devDependencies.
A package like `@ai-sdk/anthropic` is also added to `peerDependencies`.
Versions are pinned to v4 (e.g., `^4.6.0`) instead of v5 stable.

rubric.label: Zero-hard-deps public surface invariant holds
rubric.ruleStatement: The package's `dependencies` block must remain empty (or unchanged from its current OTEL-only baseline), and `peerDependencies` must not gain runtime SDK packages.
passCriteria: Run `cat packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json` and confirm the `dependencies` block is either empty (`{}`) or byte-identical to the pre-phase baseline (only OpenTelemetry entries, if any).
Confirm `peerDependencies` is empty or unchanged from baseline.
No new entry has been added that a downstream consumer of `@elenwatch/llm-http-proxy` would be forced to install at runtime.
failureExamples: `@ai-sdk/anthropic` is listed under `dependencies`, forcing every downstream consumer to install it.
A peer dependency on `ai` was introduced, forcing consumers to add it.

rubric.label: No new lockfile committed at the package level
rubric.ruleStatement: The install step must not leave a committed `package-lock.json` inside `packages/llm-http-proxy/`.
passCriteria: Run `ls packages/llm-http-proxy/package-lock.json` and confirm the file does not exist, OR confirm it exists AND is matched by `packages/llm-http-proxy/.gitignore` (or a parent `.gitignore`) so `git check-ignore -v packages/llm-http-proxy/package-lock.json` prints the ignoring rule.
Run `git status packages/llm-http-proxy/` and confirm no untracked `package-lock.json` appears.
The repo root's existing lockfile (if any) was used as the source of truth for the install.
failureExamples: A `package-lock.json` was generated inside `packages/llm-http-proxy/` and shows up as an untracked file in `git status`.
The lockfile exists but is NOT listed in any `.gitignore`, so a careless `git add .` would commit it.

rubric.label: Packages resolve, install, and type-check from package-local context
rubric.ruleStatement: After the edit, `npm install` (or the repo's chosen package manager) at the package root must succeed, the installed packages must be importable, and TypeScript must resolve their types.
passCriteria: From `packages/llm-http-proxy/`, run `npm install` (or pnpm/bun/yarn matching the committed lockfile) and confirm it exits 0 with no peer-dependency errors.
Confirm `node -e "require('@ai-sdk/anthropic'); require('@ai-sdk/openai'); require('@ai-sdk/google'); require('ai'); process.exit(0)"` exits 0 from inside `packages/llm-http-proxy/` after install.
Confirm `node_modules/@ai-sdk/anthropic/package.json` (and the other three) exists and reports a v5.x version.
Run `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/llm-http-proxy/tsconfig.json` and confirm it still exits 0.
failureExamples: `npm install` errors with `ERESOLVE` because the SDKs demand a Node version or peer dep the package doesn't allow.
A package was added to package.json but `node_modules/` was not regenerated, so `require('@ai-sdk/google')` throws `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.
Version drift causes tsc to fail because `@types/node` no longer matches what the SDKs ship.

rubric.label: No unrelated fields mutated
rubric.ruleStatement: The edit must touch only the `devDependencies` block. All other top-level fields must be byte-identical to the pre-phase state.
passCriteria: Diff `packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json` against the pre-phase version and confirm only `devDependencies` lines differ.
`scripts.test`, `scripts.build`, `scripts.lint`, `exports`, and `main` are unchanged.
No new top-level field like `overrides`, `resolutions`, or `workspaces` was added by this phase.
failureExamples: `scripts.test` was rewritten to `vitest run` while editing devDependencies.
An `overrides` block was added to force a SDK version, leaking an unrelated concern into the manifest.

phases.name: Add SDK fetch shim helper
phases.goal: Add a small helper module that exports a `createNodeHttpsFetch()` factory returning a fetch-compatible function backed by node:https.request, so SDK-issued calls route through the interceptor's patch surface.
phases.rationale: The Vercel AI SDK exposes a documented `fetch` option on each provider factory that accepts a custom fetch implementation. Passing our shim as that option makes the SDK's HTTPS calls flow through node:https.request, which IS captured by the interceptor's http.ClientRequest.prototype patch — solving the bypass-risk discovered in Stage 1.5. The shim is test-only surface (not re-exported from src/index.ts).
changes: Create src/sdk-fetch-shim.ts that exports a `createNodeHttpsFetch()` function returning a `(input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>` implementation backed by `node:https.request`; the implementation must parse the input URL, build headers from `init.headers`, write the body from `init.body`, and convert the `IncomingMessage` response into a standard `Response` object.
Type the shim's return value against the SDK's `fetch` option shape so `tsc --noEmit` validates it.
Add a file-header comment in src/sdk-fetch-shim.ts citing the load-bearing bypass-risk discovery and stating the shim is test-only surface that is NOT re-exported from src/index.ts.
inputs: src/anthropic.integration.test.ts as the horizon-7 https.request template to mirror
phases.expectedResult: packages/llm-http-proxy/src/sdk-fetch-shim.ts exports `createNodeHttpsFetch()` whose return value is type-compatible with the SDK provider factory `fetch` option and is not re-exported from src/index.ts; tsc and eslint pass on the new file.
phases.compensation: Delete src/sdk-fetch-shim.ts; no other file imports it yet at this point.

rubric.label: Shim honors the parts of the fetch contract the SDK actually uses
rubric.ruleStatement: createNodeHttpsFetch() must return a function that behaves like global fetch for the request shapes the AI SDK emits: string/URL input, POST with a JSON string body, header objects in every form the SDK produces, and a readable Response for both success and error status codes.
passCriteria: Open /Users/dimitrykatz/workspace/elenwatch/packages/llm-http-proxy/src/sdk-fetch-shim.ts and confirm the returned function accepts `input` as a `string`, a `URL`, and a `Request`-like object, and derives host/path/port/protocol from it (e.g. via `new URL(...)`).
Confirm `init.method` is forwarded (defaulting to GET when absent) and `init.body` is written to the request when present, with the request ended exactly once on every code path.

Confirm `init.headers` is normalized from all of: a plain object, an array of `[name, value]` pairs, and a `Headers` instance (e.g. by `new Headers(init.headers)` then iterating) — not only `Object.entries(init.headers)`.
Confirm the returned promise RESOLVES (never rejects) for non-2xx HTTP status codes, and that the constructed `Response` carries the real `status`, `statusText`, and the upstream response headers.

Confirm the response body is fully collected from the `IncomingMessage` (chunks concatenated on 'data'/'end', or the stream handed to `Response`) so that `await res.text()` and `await res.json()` return the provider payload.
failureExamples: The shim calls `reject(...)` or throws when the upstream returns 401/429, so SDK error handling never sees the provider error body.
`await res.text()` returns '' because the shim built `new Response(undefined, ...)` and dropped the IncomingMessage chunks.
Headers handling uses `Object.entries(init.headers)` only, so an SDK-supplied `Headers` instance silently sends zero headers and the provider replies 401.
Input is assumed to be a string, so passing a `URL` produces `[object URL]` in the request path.

rubric.label: Traffic really goes through node:https.request
rubric.ruleStatement: The shim's transport must be `node:https.request` (the surface the interceptor patches via http.ClientRequest.prototype), with no fallback to global fetch/undici that would silently bypass capture.
passCriteria: `grep -n "require\|import" /Users/dimitrykatz/workspace/elenwatch/packages/llm-http-proxy/src/sdk-fetch-shim.ts` shows an import of `node:https` (or `https`) and NO import/usage of `undici`, `node-fetch`, or a call to global `fetch(`.
The outbound call is made with `https.request(...)` and the returned `ClientRequest` is the object the body is written to.
No option is passed that swaps transports conditionally (no `if (globalThis.fetch)` style fallback branch).
failureExamples: The shim wraps global `fetch` and merely renames it, so the interceptor's prototype patch never fires.
Transport is `http.request` for https URLs, producing a protocol error against api.anthropic.com.
The shim builds its own `https.Agent` with a custom `createConnection` that bypasses ClientRequest instrumentation.

rubric.label: Repeatable per call, no shared state, no dangling handles
rubric.ruleStatement: Each call to createNodeHttpsFetch() must yield an independent fetch function, and each invocation must terminate deterministically — errors surface as rejections, and no socket/listener is left open to leak across install()/restore() cycles.
passCriteria: No module-level mutable state in sdk-fetch-shim.ts (no top-level `let`, cache object, or shared agent instance that persists between calls).
A `req.on('error', ...)` handler exists and rejects the returned promise, so a DNS/TLS failure produces a rejected promise rather than a hung test.

If `init.signal` is accepted in the type signature, aborting it actually destroys the request; if abort is intentionally unsupported, the file says so in a comment rather than silently ignoring the option.
Calling the same shim function twice in a row (two sequential requests) succeeds both times with the same result shape.
Run the package suite twice back to back: both runs pass and Jest does not warn about open handles or a forced exit.
failureExamples: A missing 'error' listener means a network failure emits an unhandled 'error' event and the test process crashes or hangs until timeout.
A module-level `https.Agent({ keepAlive: true })` keeps sockets open, so Jest reports 'A worker process has failed to exit gracefully'.
The promise is resolved inside the 'data' handler, so it resolves once per chunk and truncates multi-chunk provider responses.

rubric.label: Test-only surface, zero public/dependency impact
rubric.ruleStatement: The shim must remain internal test plumbing: not exported from the package's public entry point, and adding it must not change the package's runtime dependency footprint or the repo's lockfile convention.
passCriteria: `grep -n "sdk-fetch-shim" /Users/dimitrykatz/workspace/elenwatch/packages/llm-http-proxy/src/index.ts` returns nothing.
`node -e "console.log(require('/Users/dimitrykatz/workspace/elenwatch/packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json').dependencies)"` prints `{}` (empty runtime dependencies).
`git status --porcelain` in the repo shows no added `package-lock.json` anywhere.
sdk-fetch-shim.ts imports nothing from `ai`, `@ai-sdk/*`, or any other third-party package — only `node:https` (and optionally `node:url`/`node:buffer`).
The file begins with a header comment that (a) states the module is test-only and NOT re-exported from src/index.ts, and (b) names the bypass-risk finding that motivates it.
failureExamples: `export { createNodeHttpsFetch } from './sdk-fetch-shim'` was added to src/index.ts.
The shim imports a type from `@ai-sdk/provider-utils` at runtime, dragging a devDependency into shipped code.
The file has no header comment.
A package-lock.json appears under packages/llm-http-proxy/.

rubric.label: Type-compatible with the SDK fetch option; typecheck and lint clean
rubric.ruleStatement: The shim's return type must be statically proven assignable to the `fetch` option accepted by the AI SDK provider factories, and both repo gates must pass on the new file with no suppressions.
passCriteria: The file contains an explicit return type on `createNodeHttpsFetch()` (e.g. `(input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>` or the SDK's `FetchFunction`) — not an inferred/`any` return.
A compile-time assignability proof exists, e.g. a `satisfies` clause or a typed const such as `const _check: FetchFunction = createNodeHttpsFetch();`, so `tsc` fails if the shape drifts.
`cd /Users/dimitrykatz/workspace/elenwatch/packages/llm-http-proxy && npm run typecheck` exits 0.
`cd /Users/dimitrykatz/workspace/elenwatch/packages/llm-http-proxy && npm run lint` exits 0.
`grep -nE "@ts-ignore|@ts-expect-error|eslint-disable|: any|as any" src/sdk-fetch-shim.ts` returns nothing.
failureExamples: The return type is `any` or `Function`, so nothing catches a signature mismatch when the shim is wired into a provider factory in a later phase.
`tsc --noEmit` passes only because `// @ts-expect-error` sits above the Response construction.
`npm run lint` fails on `no-floating-promises` or `no-unsafe-assignment` in the new file.
Type compatibility is asserted in a comment instead of in code.

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is a Response that is empty or rejects on non-2xx — fix it by buffering all IncomingMessage chunks into a Buffer on 'end' and resolving `new Response(buf, { status: res.statusCode, statusText: res.statusMessage, headers: <upstream headers> })` for every status code, rejecting only on the request's 'error' event.

phases.name: Add SDK Anthropic integration test
phases.goal: Prove the in-process interceptor captures a real Anthropic Messages API call driven through the Vercel AI SDK's `@ai-sdk/anthropic` provider when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is present, and skip silently otherwise.
phases.rationale: Horizon 7's raw-HTTPS integration tests prove the interceptor captures a direct node:https.request to api.anthropic.com, but real consumers do not call node:https directly — they use the SDK. This phase closes that gap by driving the same end-to-end capture through `@ai-sdk/anthropic`'s `generateText` with the shim from Phase 2 (sdk-fetch-shim) passed as the `fetch` option to the provider factory.
changes: Create src/anthropic.sdk.integration.test.ts that mirrors src/anthropic.integration.test.ts's gate (`if (hasKey) describe(...) else describe.skip(...)`) with `hasKey` computed as `apiKey !== undefined && apiKey.length > 0`.
Read `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` env vars with fallback defaults (`https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`, `claude-3-5-haiku-20241022`).

Build a fresh `Interceptor({ providers: [parsedUrl.hostname], logger: ... })`, call `install()`, import `anthropic` from `@ai-sdk/anthropic` and `generateText` from `ai`; construct the model via `anthropic(model, { fetch: createNodeHttpsFetch() })`.

Call `await generateText({ model, prompt: 'hi' })`, then await two `setImmediate` ticks before asserting; assert `entries.length === 1`, `entries[0].url` contains `expectedUrlFragment`, `entries[0].model` contains `claude`, `entries[0].inputTokens >= 0`, `entries[0].outputTokens >= 0`, and `JSON.stringify(entries[0])` does not contain the literal apiKey.
Wrap the body in a `try { ... } finally { interceptor.restore(); }`.
inputs: src/anthropic.integration.test.ts as the horizon-7 gate + assertion template
packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json devDependencies confirming ai and @ai-sdk/anthropic are installed
phases.expectedResult: packages/llm-http-proxy/src/anthropic.sdk.integration.test.ts exists and, when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is exported, runs a single `generateText` through `@ai-sdk/anthropic` with the shim as the `fetch` option and asserts `entries.length === 1` with captured model containing `claude`, URL fragment matching the configured baseUrl, non-negative token counts, and no apiKey anywhere in `JSON.stringify(entries[0])`; without the key, the suite resolves to `describe.skip`.
phases.compensation: Delete src/anthropic.sdk.integration.test.ts; no other file imports it.

rubric.label: Per-file key gate
rubric.ruleStatement: The top-level describe must resolve to describe.skip when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is missing or empty, and to a live suite when present.
passCriteria: A top-level `const apiKey = process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (or destructure) appears before any describe.
`hasKey` (or equivalent flag) is computed as `apiKey !== undefined && apiKey.length > 0` (NOT a truthiness check on an empty string).
The describe is conditional: `(hasKey ? describe : describe.skip)(...)` OR `if (hasKey) describe(...) else describe.skip(...)` — not `describe.skip.if(!hasKey)` and not `describe.only`.
The suite compiles and resolves without throwing when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset.
failureExamples: Top-level describe is unconditional and references `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY!` inside the it() body — runs but throws at first access.
`hasKey = !!apiKey` is used, which silently downgrades an empty `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=""` to a live run with a blank key.
The describe is wrapped in a single `it.skip` whose body still runs the SDK call.

rubric.label: createNodeHttpsFetch passed as SDK fetch
rubric.ruleStatement: The shim from Phase 2 must be the actual `fetch` the SDK uses; otherwise the SDK's default global fetch bypasses node:https and no entry is ever captured.
passCriteria: `createNodeHttpsFetch` is imported from the same module Phase 2 exports (e.g. `./sdk-fetch-shim`).
The Anthropic provider is built via `anthropic(model, { fetch: createNodeHttpsFetch() })`.
The shim's return value is the value passed to `fetch:` — not stored in an unused variable.
No raw `https.request`, `http.request`, or `fetch(..., { agent })` calls appear in this file.
failureExamples: Provider is constructed as `anthropic(model)` with no options object — the SDK uses its bundled global fetch and entries stays at 0.
`createNodeHttpsFetch()` is called but its return is dropped on the floor and a hand-rolled `globalThis.fetch = ...` is patched instead.
Fetch option is wired only on a different provider factory (e.g. openai) and not on `anthropic(...)`.

rubric.label: Rollback-safe interceptor lifecycle
rubric.ruleStatement: `interceptor.install()` and `interceptor.restore()` must wrap the live SDK call so a thrown assertion, network error, or SDK rejection cannot leave the global http/https prototype patch installed and corrupt sibling tests.
passCriteria: `interceptor.restore()` appears inside a `finally` block.
`interceptor.install()` is called before the await of the SDK call and is NOT called inside the finally.
The Interceptor instance is constructed inside the test — not module-scoped and shared across `it()` blocks.
Exactly one `restore()` call per install per test — no early returns between them.
failureExamples: `await generateText(...); interceptor.restore();` with no try/finally — any failing expect() below the await leaks the patched prototype into the next test in the file.
Single module-level Interceptor reused across multiple `it()` blocks.
`restore()` lives inside `it.afterEach` but `install()` lives inside `it()` — order mismatch causes a no-op restore before any install on the first test.

rubric.label: Await two setImmediate ticks before reading entries
rubric.ruleStatement: Capture/parse/redact/emit run inside setImmediate, so the test must await two setImmediate ticks before asserting on `entries`.
passCriteria: Between `await generateText(...)` (or its equivalent) and the first read of `entries`, the test awaits `setImmediate` at least twice.
Two flush awaits are sequential in the same async function — not parallel with `Promise.all`.
No synchronous `entries.length` check appears immediately after the generateText await.
failureExamples: Single `await new Promise(r => setImmediate(r))` before reading.
`await Promise.resolve()` used instead of setImmediate — microtask flush does NOT drain the capture queue.
The flush awaits are inside a `before` hook but not inside the `it` body, so the it() races the emission.

rubric.label: No literal apiKey in JSON.stringify of the captured entry
rubric.ruleStatement: The captured entry must not contain the literal apiKey string anywhere in its serialized form.
passCriteria: A assertion of the form `expect(JSON.stringify(entries[0])).not.toContain(apiKey)` is present and runs after the two-setImmediate flush.
The `apiKey` variable compared against is the same runtime string passed to the SDK.
The assertion runs only in the live branch (the skipped branch omits it).
failureExamples: Assertion only checks headers (`entries[0].requestHeaders`) and misses a leak into body or model field.
`apiKey.slice(0, 10)` is what gets compared.
The string is checked but `JSON.stringify(entries)` (the array, not the entry) is used.

rubric.label: Entry assertions match phase shape
rubric.ruleStatement: The test must assert the four observable properties that prove this end-to-end actually fired through the right host, model, and counted tokens.
passCriteria: `entries.length === 1` is asserted (not `>= 1` — a duplicate emission would silently pass).
`entries[0].url` is asserted to contain the configured baseUrl host (default `api.anthropic.com`), read from `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` with the documented fallback.
`entries[0].model` is asserted to contain the substring `claude` (case-insensitive acceptable).
Both `entries[0].inputTokens >= 0` and `entries[0].outputTokens >= 0` are asserted.
failureExamples: `entries.length >= 1` is used — a second phantom entry from a retried SDK call passes silently.
URL fragment hardcoded to `api.anthropic.com` while ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is set to a staging host.
Token count assertion omitted.

phases.healerHint: Most likely failure: the provider is built without `{ fetch: createNodeHttpsFetch() }`, so the SDK keeps using its bundled global fetch and `entries` is empty — fix by passing the shim's return value as the `fetch` option on `anthropic(model, ...)`, not as a global patch.

rubric.label: Opt-in gate keyed on OPENAI_API_KEY
rubric.ruleStatement: The suite must run live only when OPENAI_API_KEY is exported as a non-empty string and skip silently otherwise.

rubric.label: Per-test install/restore try/finally discipline
rubric.ruleStatement: A fresh Interceptor must be installed before the SDK call and restored in a `finally` block.
passCriteria: Inside the `it` block, the test instantiates `new Interceptor({ providers: [...], logger: ... })` with no shared state across tests.

rubric.label: Two-setImmediate flush before reading entries
rubric.ruleStatement: Capture/parse/redact/emit run inside a setImmediate, so the test must await two setImmediate ticks before reading the captured `entries` array.
passCriteria: After the `await generateText(...)` call, the test awaits `await new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve))` at least twice.

rubric.label: Capture assertions cover length, url, model, and token counts
rubric.ruleStatement: The captured entry must assert the four load-bearing facts.
passCriteria: `expect(entries.length).toBe(1)` is present.
`entries[0].url` is asserted to contain both the parsed hostname (from `OPENAI_BASE_URL`) and a path segment.

rubric.ruleStatement: The literal value of `process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY` must not appear anywhere in `JSON.stringify(entries[0])`.

rubric.label: SDK packages live in devDependencies and no lockfile is added
rubric.ruleStatement: `ai` and `@ai-sdk/openai` must be installed only as devDependencies so the package's public `dependencies: {}` invariant stays empty, and the repo-wide zero-lockfile convention is preserved.

No `package-lock.json` is added anywhere under `packages/llm-http-proxy/` (or anywhere else in the repo) by this phase.

phases.rationale: Closes the SDK-gap proof for the third named provider. Gemini's `@ai-sdk/google` provider uses header auth (`x-goog-api-key`) by default rather than URL-query auth, so the no-key-in-url rubric carries over from horizon-7 unchanged.

Read `GEMINI_API_KEY` (fallback `GOOGLE_API_KEY`), `GEMINI_BASE_URL`, and `GEMINI_MODEL` env vars with defaults pointing at the Google Gemini API baseUrl and a small model id.

Build a fresh `Interceptor({ providers: [parsedUrl.hostname], logger: ... })`, call `install()`, import `google` from `@ai-sdk/google` and `generateText` from `ai`; construct the model via `google(model, { fetch: createNodeHttpsFetch() })`.

Call `await generateText({ model, prompt: 'hi' })`, await two `setImmediate` ticks, assert `entries.length === 1`, `entries[0].url` contains the parsed hostname + pathname AND does not contain the apiKey, `entries[0].inputTokens >= 0`, `entries[0].outputTokens >= 0` (allowing for the chars/4 fallback), and `JSON.stringify(entries[0])` does not contain the literal apiKey.
Wrap in `try { ... } finally { interceptor.restore(); }`.
inputs: src/gemini.integration.test.ts as the horizon-7 gate + URL-key-safety rubric template
packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json devDependencies confirming ai and @ai-sdk/google are installed
phases.expectedResult: packages/llm-http-proxy/src/gemini.sdk.integration.test.ts exists and, when GEMINI_API_KEY (or GOOGLE_API_KEY) is exported, runs a single `generateText` through `@ai-sdk/google` with the shim as the `fetch` option and asserts `entries.length === 1` with captured model id, URL fragment matching the configured baseUrl and NOT containing the apiKey, non-negative token counts, and no apiKey anywhere in `JSON.stringify(entries[0])`; without either key, the suite resolves to `describe.skip`.
phases.compensation: Delete src/gemini.sdk.integration.test.ts; no other file imports it.

rubric.label: Opt-in gate treats missing and empty keys as unset
rubric.ruleStatement: The suite must resolve to describe.skip(...) when GEMINI_API_KEY and GOOGLE_API_KEY are both absent OR both present-but-empty-string; it must run live only when at least one is a non-empty string.
passCriteria: File contains two truthiness checks (one for GEMINI_API_KEY, one for GOOGLE_API_KEY) that reject empty strings (e.g. Boolean(process.env.X) or process.env.X && process.env.X.length > 0), not a typeof/undefined-only check.
The live suite is wrapped in describe(...) or describe.skip(...) chosen by the combined gate.
GEMINI_BASE_URL and GEMINI_MODEL defaults are declared at the top of the file so the test still produces a valid hostname/path when the key is set.
failureExamples: Gate uses `process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY !== undefined` so `export GEMINI_API_KEY=""` still triggers a live HTTPS call and fails with an auth error in default CI.
Gate checks only GEMINI_API_KEY and ignores the GOOGLE_API_KEY fallback.
Gate is hardcoded to describe(...) and the test errors out when the key is missing instead of skipping.

rubric.label: Captured URL never contains the Gemini apiKey
rubric.ruleStatement: Because @ai-sdk/google sends the key via the x-goog-api-key header, the captured entries[0].url must contain the parsed hostname and pathname but must NOT contain the apiKey value as a substring.
passCriteria: An assertion reads entries[0].url and uses String.prototype.includes (or equivalent) to check it contains the parsed hostname from GEMINI_BASE_URL.
A separate assertion on entries[0].url uses expect(url).not.toContain(apiKey) so the test fails if the key leaks into the URL.
Both URL assertions run AFTER `await new Promise(setImmediate); await new Promise(setImmediate);` so the captured URL reflects the SDK's actual outbound request.
failureExamples: Test only asserts entries[0].url.includes(hostname) but never checks the apiKey is absent.
Test reads entries[0].url synchronously after generateText resolves, before the second setImmediate flush.
Test constructs the provider with `{ apiKey, baseUrl }` and the SDK falls back to query-string auth, leaking the key into the captured URL.

rubric.label: JSON.stringify(entries[0]) never contains the apiKey
rubric.ruleStatement: A defense-in-depth assertion must reject any captured entry whose full JSON serialization contains the literal apiKey value.
passCriteria: File contains an assertion of the form expect(JSON.stringify(entries[0])).not.toContain(apiKey) (or equivalent not.toMatch / regex-escape pattern).
The apiKey variable referenced in the assertion is the same non-empty value read from GEMINI_API_KEY / GOOGLE_API_KEY that was passed to the SDK constructor.
The assertion runs AFTER the SDK call resolves and the two setImmediate flushes complete.
failureExamples: Assertion is missing entirely.
Assertion uses the SDK's masked identifier (e.g. apiKey.slice(0,4)) instead of the full key.
Assertion runs before the two setImmediate ticks and asserts against an empty entry.

rubric.label: Test drives the Vercel AI SDK with the createNodeHttpsFetch shim
rubric.ruleStatement: The test must construct the model via google(model, { fetch: createNodeHttpsFetch() }) and call generateText from ai.
passCriteria: Imports include google from @ai-sdk/google, generateText from ai, and createNodeHttpsFetch from the SDK-shim module introduced in Phase 2.
Model construction passes fetch: createNodeHttpsFetch() as the second-arg options object.
Test calls `await generateText({ model, prompt: ... })` with at least one non-empty prompt string.
failureExamples: Test imports google but uses raw node:https instead of generateText, so the captured entry comes from a hand-rolled request, not the SDK.
Test omits the fetch option and relies on global fetch.
Test constructs the model with apiKey and baseUrl but no fetch.

rubric.label: Two setImmediate ticks awaited before reading entries
rubric.ruleStatement: The test must await two setImmediate ticks before asserting on entries.
passCriteria: Between `await generateText(...)` and any entries[...] access, the test contains exactly two `await new Promise(r => setImmediate(r))` calls.
No assertion on entries.length, entries[0].url, or JSON.stringify(entries[0]) runs before both ticks resolve.
The flush is local to the test body, not a shared helper that other suites might bypass.
failureExamples: Test awaits setImmediate only once.
Test awaits two ticks but then asserts on entries before the ticks resolve.
Test replaces the two-tick flush with setTimeout(..., 0).

rubric.label: Interceptor install/restore wrapped in try/finally
rubric.ruleStatement: Per-test construction of a fresh Interceptor, install() before the SDK call and restore() in a finally block.
passCriteria: Each test creates a fresh Interceptor(...) instance, calls install() once at the top, and calls restore() exactly once inside a finally block.
No code path bypasses restore() — the try body may throw without leaving the patch installed.
beforeAll/afterAll hooks are NOT used for install/restore.
failureExamples: Test calls install() but restore() is only on the success path.
Test installs in beforeAll and restores in afterAll.
Test creates the Interceptor outside the try, so a constructor exception skips both install() and restore().

phases.healerHint: The gate most likely fails because empty-string keys aren't treated as unset — fix by guarding the gate with `process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY?.trim() || process.env.GOOGLE_API_KEY?.trim()` (or equivalent) so `export GEMINI_API_KEY=""` resolves to describe.skip instead of an auth-erroring live call.
